meta.title: A day in the Gurukul · Ved Vidyalaya Foundation
meta.description: From the Gāyatrī before dawn to the evening fire: the rhythm of a day in the Gurukul, the places that hold it, and stories from the seasons of the year.

hero.h1: The rhythm has not changed in centuries.
hero.lede: The day begins in the dark and ends by firelight. In between there is recitation, grammar, mathematics, a meal cooked by the students, games in the field, and the kind of tiredness that makes sleep easy. The mathematics textbook is the only new thing in the room.

items.title: The verandah
items.body: Cool stone, open on three sides. The morning recitation happens here, and the evening one, and most of the laughter in between.

items.title: The kitchen
items.body: Run by a different group of students each week. Simple food, cooked with care, eaten together on the floor. Nothing is wasted.

items.title: The fire
items.body: The agnihotra at dawn and dusk. The students learn to tend it, and to understand what they are tending.

items.title: The garden and the cows
items.body: Vegetables for the kitchen, milk for the morning, and a daily lesson in care for living things that no classroom could teach.

items.title: The library and the computer room
items.body: Quiet, in the afternoons. The texts of the tradition on one shelf and the school syllabus on the next.

items.title: The old tree
items.body: Where the students sit to revise in pairs, where visitors are welcomed, and where, on the hottest afternoons, nothing happens at all.

stories.lede: A new student's first morning, a festival of gratitude, the monsoon on the roof. Small things, told plainly.

festivals.body: Guru-pūrṇimā, when the students thank their teachers and the teachers thank theirs. Dīpāvalī, when every lamp in the Gurukul is lit at once. The examinations by visiting scholars, which feel like a festival too. Visitors are welcome at all of them. Write to us and we will tell you the dates for the year.
